summary.prose: s4 adds three daemon requests that let a user adopt a Claude or Codex model the definitions do not list. models.check runs the family's check through its own CLI, one CLI call at a time daemon-wide, and returns each claimed effort level with the CLI's evidence; models.approve and models.reject record the user's decision for that check in the approved-model store, written atomically and acknowledged only once written. A decision takes effect at the next daemon restart, and approval is refused unless the model actually ran.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The curated cloud catalog keeps its file (src/assets/models/cloud-model-catalog.json), its loader (validateModelCatalog, src/daemon/model-catalog.ts:162) and its boot hook (src/daemon/index.ts:381), as the DEF decided, and is extended in place; the boot hook moves ahead of the settings reconcile and the worker threads, because the settings defaults now come from the file. The file is extended into the model definitions: exactly one entry for each built-in family, each with its CLI kind (CLI families), its selectable models with aliases, accepted efforts and input limit, its tier defaults and summariser model (CLI families), the Ollama tool-loop default, and the default family. Each Ollama model's input limit is its context window and replaces the global models.shaper.ollamaNumCtx; the output cap ollamaNumPredict stays global. A ModelRegistry built from the file and the per-user approved-model store answers every model question in the daemon; each thread builds it on first use and caches it, the way it loads and caches settings today (src/config/analyze.ts:234). A daemon restart guarantees that every thread uses a changed file, approval or saved tier; until then, a thread that starts or first reads them after the change, such as a worker the supervisor replaces after a crash (src/daemon/threads/supervisor.ts:136-148), may already use it, as with settings today. That is harmless: every saved tier has passed config.write's checks and every approval a check in which the model ran. The settings catalog takes the defaults of its tier runner, tier model and local coreModel rows, and the allowed effort values, from the same file, so reconcile, the updater, the settings catalog loader and older plugins keep working unchanged and no model name stays in code. One read-only request, models.definitions, serves the definitions to clients and is the source of providers.listModels; models.resolveRole lets the TUI's review command run the model the daemon would. Unknown Claude and Codex models are checked through their CLI one call at a time and recorded only on the user's approval, and only for a check in which the model ran. A tier set to a model that is neither listed nor approved runs a tier default with a warning (decision A). Tiers become global-only; a repo keeps `tasks` and coreFloor. Every Story leaves the build and tests passing, keeping a named stopgap for anything a later Story migrates. Settings-write safety is out of scope (ISSUE-8dc75bc5).

Approval is accepted only for a check in which the model ran without error. A decision applies at the next daemon restart, which the result says. Ollama has no such flow: only listed Ollama models are selectable.

boundary.internal: The per-family check procedures (Codex: the CLI's model list plus a run; Claude: a run, the input limit from the JSON output, recognised effort names), run one call at a time; telling a reachable CLI that refuses the model apart from an unreachable CLI; refusing approval unless the model ran without error; writing the store atomically and acknowledging a decision only once it is written; the method-class entries. Tests: checks against fake CLIs record each verdict and run one at a time (ac1); results list each claimed level with evidence and nothing is usable before approval (ac2); after approval and a restart only the approved levels are accepted (ac3); a rejected profile or unreachable CLI refuses the model with a reason, and approving a check whose model did not run is refused (ac4); after a restart an approved model appears in models.definitions as user-approved and a rejected one among the rejected ids (ac5); a failed store write returns write-failed and keeps the previous store.

nonFunctional.performance: The file is parsed once per thread and every model question is an in-memory lookup; models.definitions touches no CLI and makes one bounded Ollama listing call, the same one providers.listModels makes today.
nonFunctional.security: No cloud REST call is added (k1): checks run only through the installed claude and codex CLIs. The approved-model store is a per-user file under the insrc home written only by the daemon; clients reach it only through models.approve and models.reject (k2).
nonFunctional.observability: A bad file stops the daemon with a log naming the entry (s1/ac3); a dropped effort logs model and effort (s3/ac2); a tier fallback logs tier, requested model, reason and the default used (decision A); a tool-loop substitution logs both models; removing a per-repo tier override logs repo and tier (s3/ac5); each CLI call of a check and its verdict is logged.
nonFunctional.durability: Approved and rejected profiles live outside the shipped file and config.json, so they survive restarts and updates; the store is replaced atomically and a decision is acknowledged only once written; a malformed store is logged and treated as empty. When an update ships a model the user had approved, the shipped definition wins. Existing `tasks`, coreFloor, ollamaNumPredict and every tier value already in config.json are kept. Between a change and the next restart, threads may differ (a replaced worker or a late first read uses the new values); the restart brings them together.

api.name: models.check
api.signature: 'models.check': (params: { family: 'cli-claude' | 'cli-codex'; modelId: string; claimedEfforts: EffortLevel[] }) => Promise<ModelCheckResult | { error: string; recoverable: false }>  // src/daemon/model-check.ts checkModel(params, deps?: ModelCheckDeps)

parameters.name: family
parameters.purpose: The CLI family to check the model against (the family's cliKind picks the binary).

parameters.name: modelId
parameters.purpose: The model id as the CLI names it; must not be a model or alias the family already serves.

parameters.name: claimedEfforts
parameters.purpose: The effort levels the user wants to use with the model; each gets a verdict.

returns.meaning: { checkId, family, modelId, runs, inputLimit?, efforts: [{ effort, verdict, evidence }], error? } (sc4). Codex: the CLI's model list (`codex debug models`) decides each claimed effort — 'accepted' when the model's supported_reasoning_levels lists it, else 'rejected' with the listed levels as evidence (and 'rejected' for every effort when the list does not contain the model) — and one `codex exec --json -m <id>` run decides runs; no inputLimit (the CLI's own refusal decides, sc1). Claude: one `claude --print --output-format json --model <id>` run decides runs and gives inputLimit { unit: 'tokens', max: modelUsage[<model>].contextWindow }; each claimed effort is 'recognised-unconfirmed' when `claude --help` lists it among the --effort values (evidence states that no Claude CLI output shows whether the model supports it, lc3), else 'rejected' with the recognised names. Each check also records the CLI's `--version`. The result is kept in a bounded in-memory table by checkId for approve/reject.

errors.condition: family not a CLI family of the definitions, modelId empty or not a string, claimedEfforts not an array of non-empty strings, or modelId already a model or alias the family serves (registry.find).

The CLI could not be reached — runInProcessGroup's result has spawnError (e.g. ENOENT) or timedOut — error begins 'the <kind> CLI could not be reached:' — or the CLI reached its service and refused the model (claude is_error / codex error or turn.failed event) — error begins 'the <kind> CLI refused the model:' with the CLI's message.

preconditions: The daemon validated the definitions at boot.
Only one CLI call of any check runs at a time daemon-wide (a module-level serial chain); concurrent checks queue.

Every CLI call goes through runInProcessGroup (src/shared/process-group.ts:73), the exported process-group runner whose ProcessGroupResult carries spawnError and timedOut; cli-provider's private runSubprocess is not used or changed.

Run protocol (both families): the fixed probe prompt 'Reply with the single word OK.' is delivered on stdin (as CliProvider does), with cwd set to the OS temp directory and the per-call timeout. Claude: `claude --print --output-format json --model <id>`; runs:true only when exitCode === 0 AND stdout parses as one JSON envelope with is_error === false, subtype 'success' and a non-empty string result. Codex: `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only -C <tmp> -m <id>`; runs:true only when exitCode === 0 AND the JSONL stream contains a 'turn.completed' event and no 'error' / 'turn.failed' event. Classification: spawnError or timedOut → 'could not be reached'; an is_error envelope or an error / turn.failed event (whatever the exit code) → 'refused the model' with the CLI's message; any other outcome (nonzero exit without such a refusal, an envelope without the success fields, a stream ending without turn.completed) → runs:false with 'the <kind> CLI gave unreadable output: <exit code and first 500 chars of stdout/stderr>'. `--version`, `--help` and `debug models` are read only when exitCode === 0; otherwise they count as unreadable.

Claude inputLimit: modelUsage is keyed by the model the CLI actually ran (canonical id), which can differ from the requested id or alias (probe 11: --model haiku reports modelUsage['claude-haiku-5-5']). When modelUsage has exactly one entry, its contextWindow is used whatever its key; with several entries, the entry whose key equals the requested modelId is used, and otherwise the limit is ambiguous: inputLimit is omitted and the keys are logged. The canonical key is reported in the matching effort/run evidence, not substituted for modelId.
postconditions: Nothing is written: the store and config.json are unchanged (ac2).
Each CLI call and its verdict is logged.
No provider web API is called; only the installed claude / codex binaries (lc1).

api.name: models.approve
api.signature: 'models.approve': (params: { checkId: string; efforts: EffortLevel[] }) => Promise<DecisionResult>  // src/daemon/model-check.ts approveCheck(params, deps?)

parameters.name: checkId
parameters.purpose: A check this daemon ran since it started.

parameters.name: efforts
parameters.purpose: The levels the user allows; each must be one the check did not reject.

returns.meaning: { ok: true, restartRequired: true } once the store holds an approved ApprovedProfile { family, modelId, status: 'approved', efforts (the requested levels), inputLimit (from the check), decidedAt, cliVersion }; the registry, config.write and models.definitions use it after the next restart (ac3, ac5). When the check's effort discovery was unreadable or rejected every claimed level, the model can still be approved with efforts [] (it ran); no effort can be approved from such a check.

errors.condition: No pending check with that id (never run, evicted, or the daemon restarted).
The check's runs is false (unreachable CLI or refused model).
An effort is not one of the check's claimed levels, or its verdict was 'rejected'; detail names it.

The existing store is not a { version: 1, profiles[] } document (unreadable, malformed JSON, not an object, version missing, not a number or not 1, or profiles not an array), or writing / renaming the temp file failed; the previous store is kept unchanged and no file is created or replaced.

postconditions: The store is replaced atomically (write <store>.tmp, then rename) with every existing entry kept and the new profile appended; success is returned only after the rename.

api.name: models.reject
api.signature: 'models.reject': (params: { checkId: string }) => Promise<DecisionResult>  // src/daemon/model-check.ts rejectCheck(params, deps?)

parameters.name: checkId
parameters.purpose: A check this daemon ran since it started (it need not have run the model).

returns.meaning: { ok: true, restartRequired: true } once the store holds a rejected ApprovedProfile { status: 'rejected', efforts: [] }; after a restart config.write refuses a tier set to the model (s3) and models.definitions lists it among the family's rejected ids (ac4, ac5).

errors.condition: No pending check with that id.
As for models.approve; the previous store is kept.

postconditions: The store is replaced atomically with the rejected profile appended; the pending check is consumed.

dataModelChanges.details: The store s1 reads (ApprovedProfile entries, sc2) gains its only writer. The daemon appends one profile per decision; the latest decidedAt per (family, modelId) wins when the registry reads it (s1), so a later decision supersedes an earlier one without rewriting it. The document shape { version: 1, profiles: ApprovedProfile[] } is unchanged; existing entries, including ones the reader skips as invalid, are kept verbatim. Written atomically: <path>.tmp then rename, the directory created if missing. The writer accepts an existing document only when it is an object whose version is the number 1 and whose profiles is an array (the reader's root check plus the version this writer produces); a document with another version is left alone (write-failed) so a newer daemon's store is never rewritten. The new profile is validated with the reader's own profileProblem before writing.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: + writer: models.approve / models.reject append { family, modelId, status, efforts, inputLimit?, decidedAt, cliVersion }

dataModelChanges.details: A Map<checkId, { result: ModelCheckResult; cliVersion: string }> on the thread serving session methods, holding at most 32 checks (the oldest evicted). Lost on restart: an approval must follow a check run by the current daemon.

dataModelChanges.entity: Method-class table and recorded RPC set

errorCases.scenario: The family's CLI binary is not installed or not on PATH.
errorCases.detection: runInProcessGroup's result for `<kind> --version` (the first call of every check) carries spawnError (e.g. ENOENT).
errorCases.response: The check stops without further calls and returns runs:false, efforts each 'rejected' with evidence 'not checked: the CLI could not be reached', and error 'the <kind> CLI could not be reached: <spawn message>'. Logged with family, model and the spawn error.
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees why the model cannot be checked; models.approve on this check is refused with model-did-not-run (ac4).

errorCases.scenario: A CLI call hangs (no network, a login prompt, a stuck process).
errorCases.detection: runInProcessGroup's result has timedOut true (the per-call timeoutMs from ModelCheckDeps, default 120 s, fired and the process group was killed).
errorCases.response: Same as an unreachable CLI: runs:false, error 'the <kind> CLI could not be reached: timed out after <n> s'. The serial chain moves on to the next queued call.
errorCases.userImpact: The check returns an explained failure instead of blocking later checks.

errorCases.scenario: The CLI reaches its service and refuses the model (unknown model, no access).
errorCases.detection: Claude: the JSON envelope has is_error true (e.g. api_error_status 404). Codex: the --json stream contains an event of type 'error' or 'turn.failed' (e.g. model_not_found).
errorCases.response: runs:false, error 'the <kind> CLI refused the model: <the CLI's message>'; efforts keep their own verdicts (Codex list / Claude recognised names) so the user sees all evidence. Logged.
errorCases.userImpact: The user learns the model id is wrong or unavailable to their account; approval is refused (model-did-not-run).

errorCases.scenario: The CLI output cannot be parsed (no JSON envelope, `codex debug models` not JSON or without a models array, a changed CLI format).
errorCases.detection: JSON.parse throws, or the parsed value lacks the expected fields (envelope without is_error/result; list without models[]).
errorCases.response: For the run: runs:false with error 'the <kind> CLI refused the model: unrecognised output: <first 200 chars>' is NOT used — instead error 'the <kind> CLI gave unreadable output: <first 500 chars>' and runs:false. For the Codex list: every effort 'rejected' with evidence 'the CLI's model list could not be read'. For Claude help: every effort 'rejected' with evidence 'the CLI's --effort values could not be read'. Never guesses support.
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees what the check could not decide. When the run itself was unreadable, runs is false and nothing can be approved; when only effort discovery was unreadable, every level is rejected, so no effort can be approved, though a model that ran can still be approved with efforts [].

errorCases.scenario: The CLI exits nonzero, or the run's output is incomplete (Codex stream without turn.completed, Claude envelope without subtype 'success' or a result), without an explicit refusal.
errorCases.detection: runInProcessGroup's exitCode !== 0, or the parsed output fails the positive completion condition of the run protocol (Codex: no 'turn.completed' event; Claude: is_error not false, subtype not 'success' or result not a non-empty string).
errorCases.response: runs:false with error 'the <kind> CLI gave unreadable output: exit <code>: <first 500 chars>'; never treated as a successful run. Logged.
errorCases.userImpact: A model whose run did not demonstrably complete cannot be approved (model-did-not-run).

errorCases.scenario: The Claude run succeeds but modelUsage has no contextWindow for the model.
errorCases.detection: modelUsage is absent or empty, has several entries none keyed by the requested modelId, or the selected entry has no positive integer contextWindow.
errorCases.response: runs stays true and inputLimit is omitted (the CLI's own refusal then decides, as sc1 allows for a CLI model without inputLimit); logged.
errorCases.userImpact: The model can still be approved; its prompts are not pre-trimmed by a stated limit.

errorCases.scenario: The store file is unreadable or not a { version, profiles[] } document when a decision is written.
errorCases.detection: readFileSync throws something other than ENOENT, JSON.parse throws, or the parsed value is not an object whose version is the number 1 and whose profiles is an array (a missing, non-numeric or other version, e.g. {"profiles":[]} or {"version":"broken","profiles":[]} or version 2, fails).
errorCases.response: models.approve / models.reject return { ok:false, reason:'write-failed', detail naming the problem } and write nothing, so a hand-edited or damaged store is never overwritten. The pending check is kept so the user can retry after fixing the file.
errorCases.userImpact: The decision is not recorded and the user is told why; the existing file is untouched.

errorCases.scenario: Writing or renaming the temp store file fails (disk full, permissions, read-only home).
errorCases.detection: mkdirSync / writeFileSync of <store>.tmp or renameSync throws.
errorCases.response: The temp file is removed (best effort), the function returns { ok:false, reason:'write-failed', detail: the error message }; the previous store is unchanged because only the rename replaces it. The pending check is kept.
errorCases.userImpact: No partial store; the user can retry.

errorCases.scenario: models.approve / models.reject with a checkId that is not pending.
errorCases.detection: The pending-check Map has no entry for the id (never issued, evicted after 32 newer checks, consumed by an earlier decision, or the daemon restarted).
errorCases.response: { ok:false, reason:'unknown-check', detail: 'no pending check <id>; run models.check again' }.
errorCases.userImpact: The user re-runs the check; no stale result can be approved.

errorCases.scenario: models.approve on a check whose model did not run.
errorCases.detection: The pending result has runs === false.
errorCases.response: { ok:false, reason:'model-did-not-run', detail: the check's error }; nothing written; the check stays pending so it can still be rejected.
errorCases.userImpact: Approval is impossible without a successful run (sc4); the reason is shown (ac4).

errorCases.scenario: models.approve with an effort the check rejected or never claimed, or a non-array / empty-string effort.
errorCases.detection: Each requested effort is looked up in the check's efforts; a missing entry or verdict 'rejected' fails, as does a non-string entry.
errorCases.response: { ok:false, reason:'invalid-efforts', detail naming each offending effort and its verdict }; nothing written.
errorCases.userImpact: Only checked, non-rejected levels can be approved (ac3, lc2, lc3).

errorCases.detection: family is not a family whose registry cliKind is defined, modelId is not a non-empty string, claimedEfforts is not an array of non-empty strings, or registry.find(family, modelId) is defined.
errorCases.response: { error: 'invalid-params: <what>', recoverable: false }; no CLI call made.
errorCases.userImpact: A shipped or already-approved model is not re-checked; Ollama models are refused (only listed Ollama models are selectable).

edgeCases.input: Two models.check calls arrive together (two clients, or a client retrying).
edgeCases.expected: Both complete; their CLI calls run strictly one after another through the module-level chain (never two CLI children at once), each with its own checkId; a failure in one does not break the chain for the other.

The CLI calls still run (runs and inputLimit are decided) and efforts is []; models.approve with efforts [] stores a profile whose model runs with no effort passed, consistent with a ModelDefinition whose efforts is [].
Duplicates are collapsed, keeping the first order; one verdict per level.

edgeCases.input: A Codex model that `codex debug models` does not list but that runs.
edgeCases.expected: runs:true, every claimed effort 'rejected' with evidence 'the CLI's model list does not include <id>'; the user may still approve it with efforts [].

edgeCases.input: A Codex model listed with supported levels low/medium/high and claimed ['high','ultra'].
edgeCases.expected: 'high' accepted with evidence listing the supported levels; 'ultra' rejected with the same evidence, even though a run at ultra would succeed (lc2).

edgeCases.input: A Claude claimed effort 'xhigh' that `claude --help` lists.
edgeCases.expected: Verdict 'recognised-unconfirmed', evidence quoting the recognised values and stating that no Claude CLI output shows whether this model supports it (lc3); approvable.

edgeCases.input: The model was previously rejected and is checked again.
edgeCases.expected: Allowed (registry.find does not serve a rejected id); a later approve appends a newer profile and, after a restart, the latest decidedAt wins (s1), so the model becomes usable.

edgeCases.input: The store file does not exist yet (first decision).
edgeCases.expected: The insrc home directory is created if missing and a new { version: 1, profiles: [profile] } is written atomically.

edgeCases.input: The store holds entries the reader would skip as invalid.
edgeCases.expected: They are copied through verbatim; s4 never deletes or repairs entries.

edgeCases.input: A 33rd check is run while 32 are pending.
edgeCases.expected: The oldest pending check is evicted; approving it later returns unknown-check.

edgeCases.input: approve then reject (or approve twice) on the same checkId.
edgeCases.expected: The first decision consumes the check; the second returns unknown-check.

edgeCases.input: The user approves a model that a later daemon update ships in the definitions.
edgeCases.expected: Nothing in s4 changes: the shipped definition wins in the registry (sc2 durability rule).

edgeCases.input: A store at version 2 (written by a newer daemon) when a decision is written.
edgeCases.expected: write-failed naming the unsupported version; the file is not rewritten, so a newer format is never downgraded.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A check reaches the model only through the installed claude or codex binary; no provider web API and no new network client is added (lc1).
For Codex the CLI's own model list, never a successful run at a level, decides each effort verdict (lc2).

For Claude no effort is ever reported 'accepted'; recognised names are 'recognised-unconfirmed' and the evidence says the CLI cannot confirm per-model support, so only the user's approval admits a level (lc3).

The shipped definitions file and config.json are never written by s4; decisions live only in the approved-model store, in the ApprovedProfile shape s1 reads, and apply at the next restart through the per-thread registry (sc1, sc2).

The store is replaced only by an atomic rename after a full successful write, existing entries are kept verbatim, and a decision is acknowledged only after the rename; a malformed existing store is never overwritten.
LLM-reaching work is serial: at most one CLI child of any check runs at a time daemon-wide (CLAUDE.md: never Promise.all provider calls; HLD sc4 'one call at a time').

migration.stateBefore: The registry already reads the approved-model store (src/daemon/model-registry.ts readStore / buildModelRegistry, PATHS.approvedModels at src/shared/paths.ts:12) and models.definitions / config.write already honour user-approved and rejected profiles (src/daemon/model-definitions.ts, src/daemon/config-write.ts), but nothing writes the store: a user cannot adopt a model the definitions do not list, and an unlisted tier falls back to the family default with a warning (decision A). The daemon runs models through claude / codex only as providers (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:868 runSubprocess); its other spawns of those binaries are MCP registration (src/daemon/mcp-register.ts: `mcp list` / add, reached from repo.add), which run no model. Nothing checks a model the definitions do not list.
migration.stateAfter: src/daemon/model-check.ts adds the check procedures (Codex: `--version`, `debug models`, one `exec --json` run; Claude: `--version`, `--help`, one `--print --output-format json` run), a daemon-wide serial chain for their CLI calls, a bounded pending-check table, and the only writer of the store (append + atomic rename). models.check / models.approve / models.reject are registered in buildHandlerRuntime, classified 'session' in method-class.ts and pinned in RECORDED_RPC. After a decision and a restart, the existing registry, models.definitions and config.write serve the approved model or refuse the rejected one with no change to them.

Export the existing profileProblem from src/daemon/model-registry.ts (no behaviour change), then add the store writer to model-check.ts: read the current document (missing = new), refuse one that is not { version: 1, profiles[] }, validate the new profile with profileProblem, append it, write <store>.tmp and rename.
Register models.check, models.approve and models.reject in buildHandlerRuntime, add their 'session' method-class entries and add them to RECORDED_RPC.
Add the unit, contract and real-daemon tests (fake CLIs on PATH, restart between decision and use) and the gated live test.

migration.backwardCompat: Additive only: three new IPC methods; no existing request, result shape or config key changes. The store keeps its { version: 1, profiles[] } shape and existing entries are copied through verbatim, so a store written by s4 is read by the s1 reader unchanged, and a daemon rolled back to before s4 still reads it (the reader already exists). Clients that never call the new methods behave exactly as before; the UIs adopt them in s5–s7. model-registry.ts only gains an export of an existing function.

alternativesConsidered.name: Three session RPCs over an in-memory pending-check table
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: models.check runs the family's procedure under one daemon-wide serial lock and keeps the result in a bounded in-memory table by checkId; models.approve / models.reject read it and write the store atomically.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new src/daemon/model-check.ts holds the check procedures (Codex: `codex debug models` for the model's supported_reasoning_levels, then one `codex exec --json -m <id>` run; Claude: one `claude --print --output-format json --model <id>` run whose modelUsage gives contextWindow, and the recognised --effort names from `claude --help`), a module-level promise chain so only one CLI call runs at a time daemon-wide, and a bounded Map<checkId, ModelCheckResult & { cliVersion }> on the main thread. models.check (params family/modelId/claimedEfforts) returns ModelCheckResult; models.approve(checkId, efforts) refuses unknown-check, model-did-not-run and efforts outside those the check admitted, then appends an ApprovedProfile and writes the store via write-tmp-then-rename, acknowledging only after the rename; models.reject(checkId) writes a rejected profile the same way. All three are 'session' method-class entries and in RECORDED_RPC. A decision applies at restart (restartRequired:true), as the registry is cached per thread.
pros: Matches the sc4 sketch exactly (three requests, checkId hand-off)
Smallest: no new file beyond the store s1 already reads, no new stream protocol
One daemon-wide lock satisfies one-call-at-a-time across concurrent clients
Approval can only reference a check the daemon itself ran, so 'model ran without error' is enforced server-side
cons: A check is lost on daemon restart; the client must re-run it before approving (acceptable: approval should follow a fresh check)
models.check is a long-running request (one or two CLI calls, tens of seconds) with no progress frames

alternativesConsidered.name: a1 plus a persisted pending-check file
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same requests, but checks are also written to ~/.insrc so a check can be approved after a restart.
alternativesConsidered.approach: As a1, with every ModelCheckResult also written atomically to a pending-checks file under the insrc home and read back on approve; entries expire after a fixed age.
pros: A check survives a daemon restart
cons: Adds a second persistent file and an expiry policy nobody asked for
An approval could rest on a stale check run against an older CLI version
More I/O failure paths to handle
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Adds a second persistent file and expiry policy nobody asked for, and weakens the guarantee that approval follows a current check.

alternativesConsidered.name: models.check as a stream request with per-call progress
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1, but models.check is a stream handler that emits a progress frame per CLI call before its done frame.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same procedures, lock, table and approve/reject RPCs as a1; models.check registers as a stream handler emitting { phase: 'model-list' | 'run' | 'effort-names', verdict } progress frames and a done frame carrying ModelCheckResult.
pros: Clients can show progress during a long check
cons: Departs from the sc4 sketch's request/response shape that s5-s7 consume
Every client needs a stream consumer for one screen; the progress adds little for at most three calls
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Progress frames are a nicety for at most three CLI calls and depart from the owned contract's shape.

openQuestions: Checklist ep3 (partial): the serial-CLI-call invariant rests on the s1 usage.example bundle (no shared serial-queue helper; daemon code serialises provider work with sequential awaits, c12) and CLAUDE.md (c4), not on the probe evidence its s5 source id names.

Checklist alt2 (partial): s3 scored the alternatives against ac1-ac5 and sc1-sc4 but not lc1-lc3 explicitly; all three alternatives share the same CLI procedures, so lc1 (installed CLIs only), lc2 (the codex model list decides efforts) and lc3 (Claude levels recognised-unconfirmed) hold equally for each and do not change the ranking.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: How a client checks an unknown model and records the decision: every CLI call of a check goes through the daemon-wide serial chain, the result waits in the pending table, and a decision is acknowledged only after the store rename; the registry sees it at the next restart.

LldContext analyze bundles: approved-model store and registry, CLI spawning, CLI probe, RPC plug-in points, atomic writes, test patterns.
No direct cloud REST calls from our process. ... Never `Promise.all` anything that reaches an LLM provider (cloud or local Ollama embed / complete); always serial `for...of` with sequential awaits.
winnerId a1: satisfies every criterion and contract with the fewest moving parts.

codex does not reject a known level that a given model does not list (probe 4). For codex, a model's accepted levels must therefore come from `codex debug models` (probe 1), not from whether a test run succeeds.

Atomic writes follow write-to-`<path>.tmp` then renameSync (src/workflow/storage.ts:85 writeAtomic; src/config/reconcile-io.ts commit). No shared serial-queue helper exists; daemon code serialises LLM work with sequential awaits.

Every recognised level runs without a warning on every model tried (probes 8 to 10), and the output never states the effort used (probe 11). So no Claude CLI run shows whether a given model supports a given level.
